 How The Dallas Mavericks Landed Dirk Nowitzki And Steve Nash On The Same Night
 Two 1998 draft-night deals brought future MVPs Dirk Nowitzki and Steve Nash to Dallas. The trades were connected by the rights to one player.
 GA By Grant Afseth Published November 17, 2026 at 9:41 pm CST 4 min read ☆ Add us as a preferred source on Google See more of our reporting in your Google results.
 Share This Story Copy Link Email Story ↗ Story Link Phoenix Suns guard Steve Nash drives past Dallas Mavericks forward Dirk Nowitzki during the fourth quarter at US Airways Center in Phoenix on Jan. 28, 2010. (Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect) In this article Michael Finley Was Already In Dallas 
 The Nowitzki Trade With Milwaukee 
 The Nash Trade With Phoenix 
 DALLAS — Pat Garrity was a Dallas Maverick on paper for part of one night. Milwaukee took him 19th in the 1998 draft, then sent his rights and those of ninth pick Dirk Nowitzki to the Dallas Mavericks . In return the Bucks took the rights to Michigan forward Robert Traylor , whom Dallas had picked at No. 6.
 Garrity’s rights went straight into the second trade. Dallas sent them to the Phoenix Suns with Martin Müürsepp , Bubba Wells , and its 1999 first-round pick. Steve Nash went the other way. The Mavericks’ media guide records both deals on June 24, 1998.
 Don Nelson was coaching the team and running the front office. The first trade got him the young scorer he wanted from Germany. The second got him a guard he had already tried to pry away from Phoenix.
 Michael Finley Was Already In Dallas
 By then Michael Finley had been in Dallas for a season and a half. He came from Phoenix with Sam Cassell , A.C. Green , and a second-round pick on Dec. 26, 1996. Dallas sent Jason Kidd and two other players to the Suns .
 Nelson became general manager six weeks later, on Feb. 7, 1997. He took over as coach on Dec. 4, 1997. Finley started all 82 games in 1997-98 and averaged 21.5 points, and he stayed in Dallas through 2005.
 Nelson tried to get Nash during the 1997-98 season. The Dallas Morning News reported on draft night that he could not pry Nash from Phoenix at midseason and instead acquired Cedric Ceballos for Dennis Scott . That trade went through on Feb. 18, 1998.
 The Nowitzki Trade With Milwaukee
 Dallas held the sixth pick and arranged before the draft to move down to Milwaukee’s ninth pick, according to NBA.com’s Hall of Fame profile of Nowitzki. The Boston Celtics , who picked 10th, also had interest in Nowitzki.
 Nelson said the Mavericks “scouted Europe more than anybody.”
 Donnie Nelson, Don’s son, was a volunteer assistant for the international team at the 1998 Nike Hoop Summit and helped bring Nowitzki to the front office’s attention. Donnie got the international team into a Dallas YMCA to work out. Don Nelson watched Nowitzki for a full week. He called Nowitzki the most unbelievable young player he had ever seen.
 Nowitzki spent a week of the pre-draft stretch living in Donnie Nelson’s basement.
 “We hid Dirk for several weeks before the draft,” Nelson said.
 The Nash Trade With Phoenix
 Phoenix drafted Nash 15th overall in 1996. In two seasons with the Suns, he averaged 6.4 points and 2.8 assists in 141 games, according to the Suns.
 Phoenix had a condition for the Nash trade. The Dallas Morning News reported that the Suns insisted on an unprotected first-round pick. Dallas could finish anywhere in the standings and still have to give it up. It landed ninth the following June, and Phoenix drafted Shawn Marion .
 “Things could not have gone better,” Nelson told The Dallas Morning News that night.
 Nowitzki and Nash arrived in Dallas on the same day. They lived in the same apartment complex.
 A lockout delayed the 1998-99 season, and Nowitzki did not sign until the season was about to begin. He spent the extra time training in Germany with Holger Geschwindner. Nowitzki made his NBA debut on Feb. 5, 1999, in an overtime loss to Seattle. He went 0-of-5 from the field, made two free throws, and had no rebounds and four assists in 16:20.
 In a 19-31 season, Nowitzki averaged 8.2 points and 3.4 rebounds. The shot Dallas had seen in workouts took time to show up in games. He made just 20.6% of his 3-pointers as a rookie.
 Two seasons later, Nowitzki averaged 21.8 points. He and Nash were working the pick-and-pop for a team that won 53 games. The following season they both made the All-Star team.
 Nelson died Aug. 9 in Frisco. At his Aug. 13 celebration of life at Preston Hollow Presbyterian Church, Nash and Finley spoke, and Nash read a letter from Nowitzki, who was in Europe. Nowitzki’s statement after Nelson’s death, collected by NBA.com , went back to draft night.
 “You didn’t just draft me. You believed in me,” Nowitzki wrote.
 The Mavericks honor Nelson with Nellie Night on Wednesday, Nov. 18, against the Golden State Warriors at American Airlines Center. Tip-off is 7 p.m. CT.
